I did zero research on this game and bought it thinking it was "a Chinese Super Seducer" to play it with friends and have a laugh.
It's not that, it's actually "serious" even though it has its funny moments.
But even with that, this entertained us nicely for the hours it took to complete a full run through it and some extra endings.

There isn't much to say about the game, it's a "dating sim" with a romcom plot with a beginning and an end. You play as Gu Yi, a guy that is broke and in deep debt. Even then, you meet six girls who for some reason are really glad to lend you money, rent, houses, rooms, jobs, lives and in the end even their love.
The acting is not that great and the game feels really cheap despite some cool shots. 

Even then, I recommend this wholeheartedly.
My friends and I actually had tons of fun and were engaged in the story. We each had our favourite girl but since I was the one playing I went the Xiao Lu route because she is the best and sweetest girl of them all, with Zheng Ziyan a close second.
This game while far from being the best out there is a really cute and sweet read/watch and if you like this kind of games I'm sure you'll love it.

One thing I really want to stress out is to be careful to play this if you suffer from depression/loneliness and are in a bad spot overall. While it may relieve you a bit with filling that gap with 6 virtual girls showing you love in sincere forms, you may end up taking it badly, thinking "I'll never have this irl" and it may worsen your situation. If you think I'm bullshitting you, you can check Steam forums and reviews to see how, among many meme ones, there's actually some people sharing how this game affected them.
I'll admit that I also felt a bit of sadness after reflecting on it since I'm not in the best spot myself, but luckily playing it with friends made me associate mostly funny thoughts to the events of the game.

This is all ll I had to say about the game. I bought it for the memes but I actually enjoyed it quite a bit.

Oh, and for those asking, there is no NSFW content, not even hinted. And it's better this way.

I had originally started writing a review prior to finishing my first playthrough. I was about 4 chapters in when I was writing it, then had to restart my PC, forgot to submit it, and I lost it. I am glad I waited because my opinion of this game got a whole lot worse after I finished it. Be warned, this review will contain spoilers. I will put them in the spoiler text, just in case, but honestly, you are better off knowing the full truth and deciding if you still want to buy the game.

First off, let's start out with the good. All the actors portray their characters very well. They are all believable in their roles and the characters that come off as annoying are, indeed, very annoying. The videos are shot well and are framed in a way that display the first-person perspective really well. This is about all I found that was good in the game.

Now let's go to the bad. This game has a branching storyline. Sounds really nice, except for the flaw that you are required to have a certain amount of affection to proceed in the story, there are often choices that give you +1 affection with one person, and -1 affection with multiple others. There are also sections where you make a choice, which gives affection, then Gu Yi says something immediately after that ruins the moment and you lose affection. With so many neutral or negative affection choices in a chapter, you are essentially forced to focus on the character they want you to focus on in order to advance the story. In the final 3 main story chapters of the game, you have to focus on Huixin (the character I liked the least), Yueqin (the only character who I felt had a valid reason to be infatuated with Gu Yi), and Zhen. For some reason, Gu Yi is just a natural panty dropper. He just comes into contact with a beautiful woman and she can't help herself. She has to offer him help, offer him shelter, offer him her love. What does he do in return? WHO THE F KNOWS? He is really bringing nothing to the table. I felt like this was a high school boy's vision of a romance story: "Guy shows up and hot girl falls in love. He then has multiple hot girls fawning over him and he has to make a choice."

The game really gives you the illusion of choice. I decided to go after Yunsi for my first playthrough. I built up a solid relationship through the first couple of chapters. Then, in the third chapter, [spoiler]Gu Yi just acts like a jerk for no reason and just ups and leaves her. No choice in the matter. No say in anything. If you are staying at Yunsi's house, you just up and leave after she was super kind and supportive of you. You even do extra stuff that just makes her angry. I DIDN'T WANT TO DO ANY OF IT! THE GAME JUST FORCES YOU INTO IT BECAUSE THEY HAVE TO HAVE HER BE THE ONE WHO GOT AWAY! YOU ARE THEN LEFT WITH THE OTHER 5 TO CHOOSE FROM. WHAT IF YUNSI WAS MY CHOICE? SUCH HORRIBLE STORYTELLING![/spoiler]

In three of the chapters you are essentially required to cozy up to the new person who is introduced in order to get enough affection to continue down the story. It removes any agency, sets up scenes that are, I guess, supposed to be comedic relief when multiple women show up and ask you to pick from among them. There are way too many scenes where you are working with one person and then all of the sudden at least 2 or more other women show up out of nowhere and you are now in an awkward situation where you have to try and talk your way through all of them wanting you for themselves. You then make a choice that makes one person happy and the other people mad. So you have plenty of opportunities to get negative affection because of stupid, contrived scenarios. Then when you're alone with the people the game doesn't want you to be with, you can't get enough affection to proceed. This method of storytelling is so ridiculous for this type of a game. The game is supposed to be about making conscious choices to find your match through the use of storytelling, not shoehorning you into romancing people you have no affection for just because they want that character to not feel left out, or whatever their reason.

As mentioned earlier, Gu Yi just seems to be a natural panty dropper. He has no charisma, often does things that are just nonsensical for the situation, and just does things that make people angry for no reason. It's seriously a wonder that any of these women fall for him at all. The only character that actually had some reason to fall for Gu Yi was Yueqin. You can assist her to help her get rid of her ex-husband, get beaten up for her, and have a positive interaction with her child. That at least can endear you to someone in a way that makes sense. Everyone else, it's just instant attraction. Just add water. This is a very easy recommendation from me. Despite feeling bit dated, the game somehow still managed to have everything that a fmv should have (girl ranking, story/plot tree, ability to pause and unpause, etc) which is amazing as this was pretty much THE fmv that kickstarted the sudden rise of asian fmv.

The story as a whole isn't really anything too remarkable. You play as Gu Yi  who is broke and in a huge debt, but somehow™ in the midst of all of this you managed to stumble upon 6 girls who are likable, conveniently into you, and are willing to help you. Ignoring the rather unrealistic scenario, the game does do a good enough job at introducing the girls in a decent manner alongside being able to accurately portray Gu Yi's struggles whenever it does pop up, though above all, he is rather entertaining to play as, even if he can come off as being a loser (maybe even a creep?) in some situation. I'd say that the game does require some magnitude of thinking as not only does it have affection requirement in between of chapters where failing to fulfill it would resulted with the inability to progress to the next chapter, but some scenes also require you to think as Gu Yi since otherwise some choices just wouldn't ended up making any sense. Without going into spoiler territory, there's a dialogue where a girl would ask you if there's anything different that you can see about her. If you say "yes, your hairstyle have changed" then despite the game (iirc) giving you +affection for it, it isn't really the correct choice since typically MC wouldn't really notice these kind of changes, thus locking you out of one of her ending. It's a rather interesting & clever type of "gameplay" in my opinion since not only does it subvert the expectation of players where +affection = good, but it also require the players to play out the scene as Gu Yi over self-insert as yourself which makes for a fun & memorable gameplay if you do follow through with what the game wants, but if not then understandably you might be faced with frustration. In regards to the affection requirement in between chapters, I don't mind it too much since it wouldn't make sense for the girls to still be interacting and hanging out with you if you're always just be fumbling in every single interaction they have with you.

Despite all the positives, my main gripe with the game aside from heavy restrictions by the developer (online-only + no Steam family sharing) is that I wish the story would go a bit on length for the characters, using my top 3 favourite girls for example:
Xiao Lu is cool since she is about in the same exact boat as MC (in the way that both of them are broke), but her poorness isn't actually felt that much. Sure maybe she is bit hesitant to spend her money willy-nilly and is a budgeter, but there's rarely (if any) moments where she just outright can't really afford something or is being in the slums just like Gu Yi. While it wouldn't exactly be a nice sight to see, it would make the scenes feel more realistic since as of now whenever Gu Yi messes up, she would still able to cover up for him, seemingly without any repercussion.
Shen Huixin is my favourite, but it would have been a lot nicer if more of their childhood stories could be incorporated into the game since I feel like it would make a lot more sense as to why she is endlessly chasing after MC. How things work out right now is fine-ish, but some more scenes going over it would be highly appreciated.
Zhong Zhen meanwhile kinda got the short end of the stick by being introduced wayyyy later in the story. This resulted with her having the least amount of opportunity to "shine" when compared to most other girls, which generally make her the less favourable girl out of the other which is a shame since she's my 2nd favourite character.

In conclusion, despite maybe possibly coming off as rather negative in this review, I did thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game. At the end of the day, Love is All Around is nothing really too special nor great of a game, but at the same time it isn't anything too offensive either. Ultimately, I believe that if you're a newcomer to asian fmv, then I'd highly recommend starting out with this fmv as it does a good job at introducing you to the quirks and fun traits that exist in fmv. If you're a well-seasoned fmv enjoyer, well good chance that you've already played this, but if you haven't then I'd still recommend giving it a spin as it managed to capture & encompass everything that a fmv should have while managing to set a baseline of what is expected of an asian fmv, and with the game frequently going on sale despite already rocking a price tag that is more than acceptable, then it's a no-brainer purchase in my opinion.

Xiao Lu – The most normal. Works hard, cooks well, down-to-earth. Basically the definition of “wife material.” Sweet and simple.

Li Yunsi – Online friend turned real-life crush. Same hobbies, same vibes. The one with a “secret ending” and easily the most grounded. Wants the MC to commit already.

🧠 My bias ranking:
Yunsi > Zhong > Ziyan > Xiao Lu > Lin > Shen

Classic visual novel stuff—choices, routes, and time-limited decisions (light QTEs, nothing stressful).

Runs flawlessly. If your PC can run a microwave clock, it can run this.

Roughly 12 hours to see all routes and endings.

🈶 Translation
Surprisingly solid. Natural enough for the emotional beats to land, no major Engrish moments.

🎯 Final Thoughts
Is the plot dumb? Yes. Is the MC generic? Definitely.
But the girls carry the whole thing, and they’re worth it. If you want romance, drama, comedy, and a bit of fanservice, this VN checks all the boxes.

This is the OG that kickstarted the recent Chinese FMV fad. In the months and years that followed, many studios copied this concept, improved on it, and developed their own style.

And, boy, they had so much room to improve the formula, because overall this isn't a great game at all.

In terms of plot, the stories here are completely absurd. They appear serious, yet are incredibly detached from reality. Nobody in the world behaves the way these characters do. Like, nobody moves in with someone they met five minutes ago and also tolerates the other three girls already living there. In so many aspects, these characters feel very virtual and not human at all. It might have worked as a silly cartoon, but not in a seemingly realistic setting. The game pretends to explore serious themes, but fails to deliver substance in any of them. Even with the mediocre English subtitled translation you can easily tell the original dialogue must be terrible too, because even the subject matter being discussed is so constantly out of place that I can't really fault any actress for lukewarm acting, as there is only so much they could do given such absurd lines and scenarios. There is zero story nor character development across the entire game. It feels like a collection of unrelated, random scenes, made up merely as an excuse to play out cringe interactions.

With minor exceptions, most characters are obnoxious, annoying, bland, self-centered, and devoid of any charm. I found barely any incentive to interact.

This being a flowchart game you could expect some branching narratives, or at least fun choices - like every game in this genre does. Too bad! Virtually every single choice this game offers is a "pick the girl you like best and watch the rest frown" (and also watch the one you picked frown too because apparently that's very clever). There are very little properly branching segments, and they don't contribute anything meaningful to later parts of the story. So all that's left is the affection-management aspect where you need to balance each girl's love-level somewhat equally in order to unlock more chapters. Which is tedious, unrewarding, and punishes any role-play attempts.

The comedic elements are dull, cinematography is boring, locations are completely generic. I really struggle to name positives really. But the menu theme, both visual and the music, are actually pleasing. An unusually large selection of behind-the-scenes clips was a nice touch; actually I may have enjoyed watching how they filmed the movie more than the actual movie itself.

That said, this game is an artifact worth studying for historical reasons. Being familiar with it may help you appreciate newer FMV titles more, not just because many of them feature vastly better writing & direction, but primarily because they mimicked so many elements from this original that knowing it helps understand why other similarly themed games do things they way they do.

Pretty good first-person FMV romance game. You play as a gambler/artist who is in debt and struggling to find a place to stay and a job. You meet six lovely women in mostly natural ways, including being their roommate, getting hit by a car, pretending to be their husband, and meeting at an art exhibition. Rather quickly all the women come to desire you and fight for your affection, and it is easy to like each one of them for different reasons. You also have a male best friend who is pretty funny, although you might not see much of him depending on your choices. 

All the women are quite different in personality and there is actually a good number of branching paths that take you to meet up with one or another at their place or on a date. A single playthrough might take 3 hours but seeing all paths will take just as long again. You can make nearly all of them like you, and decide near the end who you want to romance. Since they're all quite great, this will probably be the default approach for many people. Note that there are quite a few avenues of failure for romance, including being killed by one of them (lol) and having them all decide to abandon you together, and deciding romance is not for you. Also cool is that each romance shows you the cold hard reality (e.g. overworked, being a father, cleaning etc) and then you can renege and go with somebody else.

There is some basic interaction with the world where you explore rooms and just click on objects to see small videos. You will also use the phone a bit, but this is just clicking to auto reply. Perhaps the most interesting form of interaction is that some of the women have a challenge sequence to get their final romance, and you have to perform actions or answer questions specifically, which can take a few tries. One of the women does not have a final romance option but you can unlock a secret ending that almost does the same thing. Good news is that going back through the branching story is pretty easy and the game seems to save on the fly so you can change a few scenes and this swaps who likes you more, then jump back to the ending.

Translation is fine overall but the menus are pretty hard to read. By default is shows scrolling comments over the top of videos (garbage) that seem to be tagged to a timestamp, and this has to be turned off manually every time as far as I know. Clicking to advance after you have seen a sequence is a little buggy as it stalls a bit. Would have liked slightly better video quality, but it's mostly fine. Also scene transitions needed to be better, because there are quite a few pauses and camera cuts. But overall an amusing and heartfelt story.

FMV dating sims are a throwback to a bygone era, but Intiny does an admirable job of updating the genre with relatively high production values, professional actors, and storylines that feel more thoughtful than the cheesy, often cringeworthy experiences of the TurboGrafx days. At its core, the game remains a power fantasy where six women compete to support your career and housing situation. However, it cleverly undercuts its hapless protagonist in ways that shift the narrative towards a wholesome (though somewhat predictable) message about taking control of your life and appreciating the people around you.

The game offers a fun, albeit idealized, portrait of modern Chinese society, introducing players to a variety of individuals and situations without feeling overstuffed or insensitive. While there are a few moments where it’s clear the writers prioritized moving the story forward over fully developing certain plotlines or characters, the sheer volume of choices—most of which are satisfying and engaging—makes up for any occasional pacing issues.

Overall, "Love Is All Around" strikes a solid balance between Chinese rom-coms and modern interactive storytelling, with enough charm and depth to keep players hooked despite its familiar premise.

这个游戏刚听闻时候，看到过于“接地气”的标题（英文名LOVE IS ALL AROUND好很多）和介绍标签，一开始是拒绝的。然而随着一些了解，和自己的游玩后，觉得这个游戏有不少可圈可点之处，乃至满足了自己的一些“梦”，也来说说感想。

这个游戏的确篇幅不长，做工也不算很精致，特别每个转场停顿看着有些生硬。不过在于几个女演员的挑选上下了功夫，她们不算倾国倾城，不过都很符合角色的定位，演技台词也都可以。

很多人说这个游戏科幻，我觉得其实也不是都如此。不过我也理解了为何会被说成科幻，乃至作为卖点。

主角没有露脸，但是就游戏里面的各种信息来看，这个角色并不是那么的一无是处。他表面欠债几百万，钱都还不起。但是很多对话看得出，他家里家境不差。有艺术天赋，学过正规的画画。拳击可以打败林乐清的前夫，也看得出身材够壮有一定的锻炼。还有老六那句“你不比以往”自己说的“以前没把钱当钱”都可以看出他家境不差。是一时做生意失败，不想靠别人帮忙。债主还是青梅竹马小女友的老爹，并没有逼着他支付，只是不希望女儿和他好而已。

同时主角在大部分的分支里也很热心乐于助人，也很有自尊心。也就是长相有人吐槽过，但主要是那个前夫，还有沈彗星的闺蜜，可能他只是看着不够威猛。

这样的男生在有详细剧情描写的情况下，和剧中任何一个女角色发生感情，都是合乎情理的。只是6个人，彼此还不怎么吃醋闹，才显得科幻。特别是开头和郑梓妍的相遇的确比较扯，极大程度放大了这种印象。说科幻的，不少都拿这段来举例。

郑梓妍作为女一号，就是典型爱情故事里那种cipher式的天降女主。身份神秘，顾虑少极其看重爱情，在男主角低落的时候出现带来无尽光明。紫霞那么被人喜欢也因为她是这种类型。但是这个开头实在处理的不好，就因为穿件衣服就去喝酒了，如果改成主角低落时在酒吧里为她出头，这样会合理的多。虽然这就和后面林乐清重了。其实之后对她也做了一些诠释，她过去的恋爱结果都不好，但是看着还是太二次元化太虚幻了。这个角色本身塑造不错，很讨人喜欢，但是也同时放大了科幻感，特别和其他人对比。

其他几个女角色就要更现实不少，比如肖鹿作为来社会打拼的单纯少女，能受到哥哥那样的关怀动心是合理的，虽然进展还是略快。沈彗星和男主是青梅竹马却打不破那一层，所以把男主落魄看成自己成功的机会。林乐清虽然条件好，但是有儿子，有纠缠不休的前夫和家庭，有个能包容他的男人不容易。

钟甄这个角色被人说太简单，我觉得更多是追求过程太快太容易了，她自身的塑造还是有点料的，比如不安全感（后面的摊牌也看得出她有要求），工作之外感到枯燥，被人追求倍增压力。现实的女霸总自然没那么简单，但是同样，女频文的男霸总，也和现实里差别很大。

这个游戏这点也做的好，它不仅是让玩家感受到被爱，也让这些女角色各自展现的脆弱和烦恼。这样既不让她们爱显得完全是无根之木，也能让主角用自己的行动和爱帮助她们，同时实现自身的成长，去承担责任和关怀他人。这其实也是对于很多玩家的心理满足。好比樱木花道对赤木晴子的追求和对篮球的爱，本质上是为了脱离原本浑浑噩噩的生活，通过打拼得到大众的认可。爱是相互的，不是单方面的索取。

其他男角色也没有都丑化，虽然追求钟甄的总裁还有林乐清的前夫不是很正面的形象，但是李云思的未婚夫就是挺好的人。老六更是铁杆好兄弟。

李云思放最后说。我之所以会买这个游戏，主要也是因为李云思。因为事先知道她是附加结局，在之前的结局选择，我是有些别扭的，因为不想渣别人，选择上是根据“最能经受打击的”那个来的。所以肖鹿这种天真小姑娘是坚决不碰的，林乐清也是有个孩子不容易，最后还是委屈一下钟甄了。虽然本身钟甄也是第二人选。

这种大姐姐本来就是我的菜，但是之前也见过很多，演员气质不错算不上倾城倾国。能让我投入有一个极其重要的原因：志趣相投。

我不是一个特别渴望爱的人，相反更希望找到一个心目中完美的女神去投入自己所有的爱，哪怕没有回报。我有很多喜欢的文艺女角色，也追过很多女明星女运动员，从她们的作品、比赛、自传都看，去读她们或者她们角色的灵魂。乃至追求过现实里的一些美女。她们的灵魂大多也是同样美丽的，不少人都有着传奇的人生。但是这么多女神里，和我有类似兴趣，喜欢我爱的那些文艺IP和体育的非常少，甚至大部分是绝缘。包括女足球员里皇马球迷也极少。虽然这不是不喜欢她们的理由，但是多少也是有些遗憾。对瑞典女足球员阿斯拉妮的崇拜，也因为她是皇马铁杆。

而李云思除了温柔大姐姐的性格之外，她毫无疑问是最懂主角的，不仅知道主角的向往，欣赏主角的天赋，默默支持希望帮他成功，不让他过分在意俗务。同时她也和主角有相同的艺术爱好，还能看到主角关注艺术背后的人文精神。这一点，其他女角色显然了解得不够深入。

而且她也展露出了相对独立的人格。她的离开，最主要并不是因为主角和其他人纠缠不清，而是主角为了俗务放弃了艺术，和她所欣赏的他越来越远。因而她也一度选择了别人。

同时只有主角自己做出努力去求爱，加上之前的网络沟通让她看到主角的追求和见识，才在最后彼此都坚持到底。据说李云思没有独立结局是因为疫情等原因，但是现有的结局也别有一番韵味。比其他的一帆风顺更美，更搭她。这种爱是我所渴求的。所以她既然做出了这样难得的放弃，自己也值得为她放弃。

从李云思的身上，我看到了大姐姐那种默默的关怀支持，更有对于主角才艺和灵魂上的理解。而且她对主角的情感，同时也是对于自己艺术梦想的爱。从她身上，我不仅看到了自己寻找千百度的“她”，也看到了那个渴望知己的“我”。因而这个角色非常的打动我，让我买下这个游戏，从中得到了很多情感上的满足，甚至甘愿许诺他人后再离开。当然，戏是戏人是人，演员自己也说和角色没有多少相似，但还是感谢她的表演，给我带来的快乐。

总体而言，这个游戏虽然有不少粗糙之处，但是的确有明显的长处。只是被很多偏见所掩盖了。包括这段时间的正面宣传，也有一些过分强调了对玩家被爱的满足，忽略了它对于女角色本身的刻画，以及对于主角自身成长都有不少可圈可点之处。写下这篇出了发表自己的感想，也希望能帮大家更好了解这个游戏的长处。

About two weeks ago, out of instinctive curiosity, I played the game "Love is All Around." It made me feel fantastic when I played it the first night. It's unbelievable to experience a life filled with all kinds of beauty around you. For many men who have never tried talking to any girls, this could be the best game for them to experience life as a handsome and charming man (though the debts in the game are quite heavy).

In the game, there are six girls with different personalities, and all of them fall in love with you (of course, you need to choose the right answers to make them like you). But in reality, you can't have all of them like you; you need to make a decision. There are six good endings in this game, but to me, I like none of them. You can choose the poor but positive girl who even motivates you to compete in a money-saving competition with her. If you don't like paying and working hard, there are other girls who own their own houses and can help you pay off all the debts. One of them is the creditor and also your childhood sweetheart, she is full of enthusiasm and a bit arrogant. One is a boss who manages a company, she is very rich but busy. One is the girl who silently helps you, never throwing a temper, and provides you with practical help. One is the sexiest and the second richest girl but has a son living with her; she always needs you to understand her family, including children and elders. Finally, the most popular among players, she is the girl you met first, and the most dangerous (if you do something wrong, she may "kill" you). She loves to drink and party, she is independent and free-spirited. They are like mirrors reflecting reality, both real and unreal.

You can enter each girl's ending if they like you, but before the end, the girl you choose will confess her shortcomings to you and give you another chance to choose a better girl without those shortcomings. If you don't like the ending, you can stop and reconsider.

I felt very tired when I finished all the endings of the game. Although the story in the game may not be true, the art in it draws from life. The craziest thing is that real life can be even more dramatic. I felt upset when I tried to put myself in those situations. I couldn't understand why we need to abandon something to find love. I don't want to experience this feeling, even if it may never happen to me. Actually, my favorite ending is living in a rental house with my friends and trying to pay off the debts.

My sister told me that it's fine; I am still at an age where I don't want to be in a relationship. I am living alone now, feeling free and happy. Maybe I will understand love in the future, but for now, let me enjoy the night with myself.

Good night. 💤

Love Is All Around is one of the first FMV games I ever played, and to me, it remains one of the most iconic titles in Asian FMV history. It didn’t just introduce me to the genre; it helped define what modern Chinese interactive storytelling could be. The game’s success proved that FMVs can be cinematic, emotional, and commercially viable, inspiring many studios across Asia to follow its path.

What really works is how genuine it feels. The game blends romance and realism without overdoing either. Every choice and moment feels grounded, enhanced by the soft visuals and calm soundtrack that make it easy to get lost in its world.

That said, not every route lands perfectly. Some storylines, particularly Li Yunsi’s, feel underdeveloped, and a few late-game choices can come off as forced or emotionally inconsistent. Still, the sincerity of its writing and the beauty of its presentation make it a deeply memorable experience.

In short, Love Is All Around is a heartfelt and beautifully crafted FMV that captures the emotional essence of modern Asian romance and continues to resonate long after the credits roll.

I enjoyed it enough to do a second or third play-through to get some extra routes/endings.

This game has one really major flaw.  It seems that there's really only one correct path to finish the game.  The way the game is set up, is that it is done in chapters.  You have to increase the affection of the girls in each chapter to reach a certain goal.  If you don't meet that goal, you don't advance.  The problem here is that there seems to be one set way to reach that goal.

For example:  I've played this game up to chapter 5 and then got stuck.  A friend wanted to watch me play so I decided to start over.  Got through chapter 1 fine.  Chapter 2 however, I could not get any further even though I made all the same choices I made the first time I played.  I went back, chose different girls and all of their options and still could not get past chapter 2.  The only thing I could think of is that I made a different choice in chapter 1 that changed the starting conditions of chapter 2 preventing me to get the required points to move on.  This really is a crappy game mechanic.

On the plus side, the girls are cute.
